title: The life of a file on ext4
question: A file is created, written, made durable, closed, and deleted: one syscall at a time. What does ext4 do at each step?

stops.note: The name is not there, and O_CREAT: ext4 makes the file, all in one journal transaction.
A free inode: find one in a block group's inode bitmap, and mark it used.
The name "note.txt": into free space in a block of the directory, next to the other names.
The bytes go into the page cache, and the page is marked dirty. Nothing is on the disk yet.
Delayed allocation: no disk block is chosen yet; one is only reserved.
Now the data must reach the disk.
Write the dirty page back: the multiblock allocator picks it a free block, from the block bitmap.
The journal (jbd2, its own thread) commits the metadata changes: the bitmaps, the inode, the directory block.
The block layer: an I/O request to the disk, /dev/loop0, whose blocks are a file in memory.
The last reference to the open file goes. The file stays: it still has a name.
The name leaves the directory block (its space joins the entry before).
No names and no users left: the inode is evicted...
... its data block goes back to the block bitmap...
... and the inode to the inode bitmap.
